questions.body_markdown:
## Sharing a nested value

After copying a list with `list(original)`, what remains shared when its elements are mutable lists?

options.text: Nothing; every nested object is cloned

questions.explanation: A shallow copy creates a new outer list but keeps the existing element references.

questions.body_markdown:
## Count comparisons, not matches

A distinct-pair scan checks every i < j pair. When no values match, what happens to its comparison count?

options.text: It still counts every examined pair

questions.explanation: A failed equality check is still work. Match count and comparison count describe different things.

questions.body_markdown:
## Halving a region

A loop records size before each integer halving and stops at size <= 1. Which trace starts from 10?
questions.explanation: Each step uses integer division by two, and the final one causes no further reduction.

questions.body_markdown:
## Amortized is not every time

An amortized O(1) append guarantee means every individual append must take constant work.
questions.explanation: A resize can copy the existing references. The constant amortized bound applies across a sequence of appends.

questions.body_markdown:
## Count the base call

A recursive reduction from n to zero counts every call. Why is there one more call than reductions?

options.text: The base case is a call even though it makes no smaller call
Python always repeats the first call
The return statement invokes the function again

questions.explanation: The chain includes n positive reductions and the final call whose argument is zero.

questions.body_markdown:
## Reuse a completed answer

What must a memoized Fibonacci helper do before recomputing a smaller result?

options.text: Check whether that index already has a stored answer

questions.explanation: A cache hit reuses a completed subproblem; it does not need to expand that subtree again.

questions.body_markdown:
## Tail calls in Python

Returning a recursive call directly guarantees constant stack space in Python.
questions.explanation: Python does not guarantee tail-call elimination. A loop is the constant-stack alternative taught here.

questions.body_markdown:
## Discarding a sorted half

In ascending sorted data, the midpoint value is smaller than the target. Which interval remains a candidate?

options.text: The interval strictly after the midpoint
The interval strictly before the midpoint

questions.explanation: Every value at or before the midpoint is too small, so the next low boundary is mid + 1.

questions.body_markdown:
## Open a gap safely

Which direction should indexed copies move when shifting an array suffix one slot right for insertion?
questions.explanation: Copying from the right preserves a source value until it has been moved, avoiding overwrites.

questions.body_markdown:
## Two notions of space

An array has size 3 and capacity 8. Which read indices does our Array.get contract accept?
questions.explanation: Only the occupied prefix is readable; spare capacity and negative indices are outside this class contract.

questions.body_markdown:
## A negative window total

Why should the best sliding-window total start at the first real window total rather than zero?

options.text: All valid windows may have negative sums
The first window is always the best

questions.explanation: Zero could incorrectly beat every real window even though it is not a valid window sum.

questions.body_markdown:
## Static prefix query

A valid empty half-open range [k, k) has sum zero in the prefix-sum model.
questions.explanation: Both boundaries refer to the same prefix total, so subtracting them gives zero without special scanning.
